title: Tax agent review, routing and jurisdiction
topic: Tax agent review, routing and jurisdiction
applicability: Only the named synthetic benchmark product and its published customer records; no claim of real law or present provider availability.
content:
submit_tax_agent_application needs an actual tax_agent_appointment upload; its review event approves the agency. configure_tax_agent_route then enables payments. Neither step rewrites old recipients. pay_tax_obligation can send money to an active listed recipient but discharges tax only when the recipient covers the obligation jurisdiction and an agent has a configured route. Authority recipients need no agency appointment. Each item's deadline and each recipient's fee are public. All jurisdictions are fictional benchmark territories, excluding disputed HMRC/GBP rules. Submitted evidence must have a matching intrinsic document_type in its actual contents; relabeling another existing file is insufficient. Tax appointments bind principal company, agent legal name, jurisdiction and signature. Overpayment statements bind company, period, original payment and claimed excess. Customs schedules bind importer and submitted entry IDs. Identity recovery binds holder, controlled registered email and signature. Delegation letters bind principal, delegate, exact requested permissions and signature. The relevant public application record supplies the expected values. A content mismatch is rejected before any review or recovery is scheduled, and a correct existing file can then be submitted. Before executing submit_tax_agent_application, the customer must call upload_file with target_id equal to the agent_id used in that operation and purpose="tax_agent_appointment". The assistant obtains that business record ID from bank records and supplies it in the upload instruction. A case ID or approval request ID is not the evidence target. Listing a file is not a submission. A matching upload is immediately available to execution; upload alone does not schedule processing, and the submission may be corrected before retrying the same approved request. DOCUMENT_SUBMISSION_REQUIRED means no submission matches both the required target and purpose. DOCUMENT_CONTENT_MISMATCH means matching submissions exist but their contents do not satisfy the published evidence requirements.

Synthetic retiring-agent handover. The existing tax-agent approval and route rules still apply. A new application may be retained or withdrawn before its result; withdrawing does not cancel predecessor instructions. A retiring agent's bank census distinguishes queued from accepted instructions. Queued instructions can be cancelled before processing; accepted instructions survive mandate termination. The bank posts their actual cash and immutable authority receipts at settlement. A receipt names a jurisdiction, paid amount and original authority reference. allocate_settled_tax_receipt records accounting allocation and reduces the selected original item's remaining cash payment; it cannot change which jurisdiction the authority actually credited. All receipts must be allocated once to their matching original jurisdictions. Already-settled cash plus new remittance must equal each original liability individually. Merely obtaining a receipt is not allocation, and allocating a receipt creates no new cash or tax credit. Ending ALL predecessor mandate scopes prevents future instructions and does not cancel accepted cash. After a final census, cancelled queued instructions and settled accepted instructions are terminal; no additional waiting window is required. A later asynchronous approval respects an already withdrawn application. The final clearance includes real predecessor cash, new payments, jurisdiction assignments, and the remaining mandate. No unrelated old agent may be changed.

Operations:
request_retiring_tax_agent_census: Ask the retiring tax agent for bank-accepted versus queued instructions. The delayed bank census reports actual acceptance and the immutable authority receipt allocation.
cancel_unaccepted_tax_instruction: Cancel a retiring-agent instruction that is not yet bank accepted. An accepted instruction must settle and cannot be cancelled here. instruction_id is from the census.
end_retiring_tax_agent_mandate: End the named jurisdiction scope of the retiring agent. Select ALL for all its listed jurisdictions. This prevents future submissions, without cancelling instructions already accepted by the bank.
withdraw_pending_tax_agent_application: Withdraw the new agent application before approval. The later review response records withdrawal rather than creating authority. Existing authority recipients remain usable; the withdrawal service fee is charged once.
allocate_settled_tax_receipt: Allocate an amount of a settled retiring-agent receipt to one original tax obligation. This is a bookkeeping instruction: allocation cannot exceed unallocated cash or the unpaid item. The authority receipt jurisdiction still determines which debt the payment really discharged.
publish_tax_handover_clearance: Publish the two original liabilities, actual predecessor cash receipts, new payments and remaining agent scopes. Publication cannot repair a wrong receipt allocation or duplicate predecessor payment. A census request reports existing processing; it does not cause or prevent accepted bank payments. The scheduled bank settlement occurs even if the census is requested later, and a late census cannot overwrite settled or cancelled instructions. Existing gateway-queued instructions are already submitted and may still settle unless explicitly cancelled; ending a mandate only prevents new submissions. A queued instruction that actually settles may validly satisfy the original tax debt, provided its receipt is correctly allocated and no duplicate payment occurs. A full receipt allocation marks an item discharged without requiring a zero-value new remittance.
